posts.content: Pau Labarta Bajo View Pau Labarta Bajo’s profile • 3rd+ Building and teaching AI that works ​> Maths Olympian​> Father of 1.. sorry 2 kids 1d • 1d Visible to everyone Stop wrestling with fine-tuning scripts cobbled together from 5 different repos. Here's something better ⬇️ We open-sourced leap-finetune, your go-to tool to fine-tune LFM models by Liquid AI One library. SFT. DPO. VLMs. MoE. 100% Open Source. 𝗕𝘂𝘁 𝘄𝗵𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹? Fine-tuning small models is the most underrated skill in AI right now. A 1.2B model fine-tuned on your data beats GPT-4 on narrow tasks. Costs pennies. Runs anywhere. But the tooling has been a mess. You grab TRL from here, Accelerate from there, hack together some Ray scripts, pray your YAML configs don't conflict. leap-finetune fixes this. 𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁'𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗲? → Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) → Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) → Vision-Language Model fine-tuning → Mixture of Experts support → LoRA out of the box → SLURM integration for cluster jobs Works on a single GPU. Scales to 8x H100s without changing your code. It even runs on serverless GPUs on Modal 𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗼 𝗿𝘂𝗻 𝗶𝘁? Git clone the repo, edit your configuration, and then uv sync uv run leap-finetune config.yaml That's it. Built on Ray Train + Accelerate + TRL. Ready for production. Enjoy ↓ https://lnkd.in/dEzmS9xD PS: Thoughtful PR contributions are really welcome

posts.title: Lan Chu View Lan Chu’s profile • 2nd AI Tech Lead | Senior Data Scientist | Work with LLMs before they were cool 1d • 1d
posts.content: Lan Chu View Lan Chu’s profile • 2nd AI Tech Lead | Senior Data Scientist | Work with LLMs before they were cool 1d • 1d Visible to everyone I tried to run Claude Code with an open source model Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. Zero API costs. Local inference. Same Claude Code workflow. When I run out of tokens with Claude Code, I sometimes feel like a deer in headlights. Especially when debugging, I don’t want to manually shift through my code base, because that is what AI is for. Now that local models are getting better, I gave it a try on a Macbook M1 32GB to see if it’s a nice alternative. The setup works with any open model e.g Qwen3.5, DeepSeek, Gemma. My setup consists of using llama.cpp to run the model as a service and connecting it to Claude Code. Setting it up takes about 15-20 minutes, of which the majority of the time is waiting for the download of a 30B model to complete. Qwen3.5 is currently the strongest agentic and coding model trained for long-horizon reasoning, complex tool use, and recovery from execution failures. My first impressions: 1. 𝐈𝐭 𝐢𝐬 𝐬𝐥𝐨𝐰! An M1 chip is clearly not as fast as a top tier NVIDIA video card. With a local model, you start to notice how much of the experience depends on speed, not just quality. Took almost 5-10 minutes of thinking to identify a bug. This is not very practical. 2. 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐱𝐭 𝐢𝐬 𝐚 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐥 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐭 𝐥𝐨𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲. The context window is the bottleneck. The model natively supports 262K tokens, but locally you are constrained by your available RAM. Tokens fill up fast when Claude Code is reading multiple files and keeping tool call history. 3. 𝐈𝐭 𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐢𝐭𝐞 𝐬𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐭 (as first impressions): although the ttft is a bit long, it works rather well otherwise. I threw a few bugs at Qwen3.5-35B and it diagnosed them correctly and implemented working solutions. For refactoring or complicated features, I wouldn’t trust it yet, need to test more. Overall I definitely see the value, and while it is definitely not a replacement for something like Opus 4.5, it is exciting to see small language models getting better and more accessible. I wonder how the large open weight models compare to Opus 4.5 though. Is it perhaps time to buy a mac studio and try out the 397B version of Qwen3.5. What do you think? Want to set it up yourself? Link to step-by-step guide in the comment. ⬇️

posts.content: Pau Labarta Bajo View Pau Labarta Bajo’s profile • 3rd+ Building and teaching AI that works ​> Maths Olympian​> Father of 1.. sorry 2 kids 2d • 2d Visible to everyone "LLMs just memorize. They're not really intelligent." My answer: I don't care. Consider drug discovery. Drug discovery is the process of finding molecules that treat disease. Every medicine you've ever taken started here. Finding molecules that treat disease. But here's the problem: It takes 10 to 15 years. Costs billions. Over 90% of candidates fail in clinical trials. Why? Because most of the work is trial and error. Synthesize, test, fail, repeat. Each iteration costs months and millions. But the thing is, the data to make better predictions exists. But it's scattered and high-dimensional. No human can hold the full picture. A model trained on this data can. It compresses that space into weights. 𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗲𝘅𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲 A new paper from Insilico Medicine and Liquid AI trained a 2.6B parameter model on 120 billion tokens of pharmaceutical data. It matches or outperforms models 10x its size. It beat TxGemma-27B on 13 of 22 ADMET tasks. It outperformed GPT-4.5 and Claude Opus on affinity benchmarks. 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗲𝘃𝗮𝗻𝘁? 2.6B runs on a single GPU. On-premise. Infrastructure a startup can afford. We're not waiting for AGI. We're waiting for pattern matchers good enough, trained on the right data, small enough to deploy anywhere. That future is here. Link to the paper in the comments 👇
